title: A frame arena
description:
Games often allocate scratch memory for one frame from an **arena**: a single block from which pieces are handed out by moving an offset forward, and which is reset all at once at the end of the frame.

Complete the class `Arena`. Its constructor receives the size of the block in bytes. Instead of real pointers, it hands out **offsets** into the block, which keeps the task easy to test.

- `allocate(size, align)` returns the offset of a new piece of `size` bytes, starting at the first offset at or after the current position that is a multiple of `align`. It moves the position to just after the piece. If the piece would not fit, it returns `-1` and changes nothing.
- `used()` returns the current position.
- `reset()` moves the position back to 0.

`align` is always a power of two: 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16.

```
Arena a{ 64 };
a.allocate(3, 1)   -> 0     (bytes 0..2)
a.allocate(4, 4)   -> 4     (skips 3 to reach a multiple of 4)
a.allocate(8, 8)   -> 8
a.used()           -> 16
a.allocate(64, 1)  -> -1    (does not fit; nothing changes)
```
hints: First work out where the piece would start: the current position rounded up to a multiple of `align`.
For a power of two, `(position + align - 1) & ~(align - 1)` rounds up. Adding `align - 1` pushes any remainder over the next multiple, and the mask clears the low bits.
Check that the piece fits before changing anything: the start must not be past the end, and `size` must not be more than what is left after the start.
lessonTitle: The Heap: Asking for Memory at Run Time
